correctness.rationale: The proof first partitions a minimal dominating set in a connected cubic graph into isolated and nonisolated selected vertices. Each nonisolated selected vertex has a distinct external private neighbor. Counting three edges from every isolated selected vertex into the residual outside class proves |S|≤N/2. Equality forces either an independent bipartition side or a perfect-matching cut. On C_n□K_2, independent sides are exactly two alternating sets when n is even. A matching cut either splits every rung coherently (the two layers) or has monochromatic rungs in cyclic runs of length exactly two (four phases only if 4 divides n). These exhaustive cases are pairwise distinct and all minimal dominating. Every quantifier n≥3 and the n=3,4 boundaries are addressed. Independent subset enumeration n=3..10 and bigger-size tests n=3..8 corroborate the proof; no finite computation is used to infer the infinite conclusion.

value.rationale: Upper domination on Cartesian grid products is an active motivated invariant. The result completely classifies maximum-size inclusion-minimal dominating vertex sets, rather than merely recovering the already known bound or reporting one example. The exact count exhibits a sharp four-periodic boundary: the number of optimizers jumps from 2 to 4 to 8, with additional matching-cut configurations existing precisely when 4 divides the cycle length. The classification distinguishes nonbipartite odd prisms from bipartite even prisms and gives a structural interpretation of every extremizer. This exact natural infinite-family census is substantive even without a downstream general theorem.
